h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ships in Durrës, Albania
intro: Durrës is Albania's largest port and its main ferry link to Italy, with ro-pax ships crossing to Bari and Ancona alongside container, bulk and general cargo traffic. Ships here make working calls and there is no large drydock in the port, so gauging is done alongside or at anchor. Atlantis NDT plans each Durrës job around the ship's sailing schedule and Albanian entry requirements, with the thickness measurement team travelling from India.
keywords: ultrasonic thickness measurement for ships in durrës

highlights.p: Ro-pax ships run year-round between Durrës and the Italian ports of Bari and Ancona, with a strong summer peak, and their vehicle decks, ramps and ballast tanks can be gauged in stages across turnarounds.

Containers, dry bulk and general cargo for Tirana and the wider region pass through Durrës, giving defined gauging windows on container ships, bulk carriers and general cargo ships during or after their cargo calls.
With no large drydock in Durrës, owners dock ships in Italy, Croatia or Greece, and gauging at Durrës beforehand gives the chosen yard a steel estimate before the ship sails across the Adriatic.

port.h: The port of Durrës and its ferry and cargo traffic
p: Durrës, on the central Albanian coast west of Tirana, is the country's largest port and its principal gateway for both passengers and cargo. Ro-pax ferries run year-round to Bari and Ancona in Italy, carrying passengers, cars and freight trailers, with traffic rising sharply in summer as Albanians living abroad travel home. The commercial port handles containers, dry bulk and general cargo for Tirana and the rest of the country, and is the sea gateway for a hinterland that reaches by road towards Kosovo and North Macedonia.

The ferry fleet drives much of the inspection demand. Ro-pax ships on the Italy routes work intensively through the summer peak and are docked in the quieter months, and their vehicle decks, ramps, stern doors and ballast tanks carry the wear of years of trailer and car traffic. Because Durrës has no large drydock, ro-pax ferry gauging here is done alongside, usually in the hours a ship spends in port between crossings, either to give owners pre-docking estimates or to close out items before a docking in Italy, Croatia or Greece. Container and bulk ships bring short, defined scopes during cargo work. Thickness measurement in Albania is therefore mostly a matter of working calls rather than yard stays.

Durrës is also a port in transition. Albania has announced plans to move commercial cargo to a new port at Porto Romano, north of the city, and to redevelop parts of the old harbour as a marina and waterfront, although the timing of the new port has shifted more than once. For a superintendent, that means checking with the agent which berth a ship will use and what access arrangements apply at the time of the call. When ships wait at anchor off the port for a berth, condition gauging by launch becomes practical and can use time that would otherwise be lost.

facilities.h: Where thickness gauging happens in the port of Durrës
p: Gauging in Durrës is done afloat. At the ferry berths, ro-pax ships can be gauged between arrival and departure, with vehicle decks, ramps and the ballast tanks below them the usual focus; on overnight services the daytime stay alongside gives a working window of several hours. At the commercial quays, container ships give access to hatch covers and ballast tanks during cargo work, and dry cargo ships open their holds to the team once discharged. The ship's agent arranges port passes and coordinates timing with the berth operator. Where a ferry calls on a fixed weekly pattern, the berth and access arrangements usually repeat, which simplifies planning across several visits.

Ships at anchor off Durrës are reached by launch through the agent, which is the usual route for pre-purchase, on-hire and off-hire gauging. For full docking programmes, owners use yards elsewhere: across the Adriatic in Italy, along the Croatian coast, or in Greece. Hull gauging in Durrës before the ship leaves gives the yard a steel estimate for its specification, and the same team can be mobilised to the yard for the docking itself, which keeps measurement locations and methods consistent.

Container quays — feeder container ships gauged on hatch covers and coamings, with ballast tanks added when the crew can make them safe
Bulk and general cargo quays — holds, hatch covers and ballast tanks gauged on dry cargo ships once their cargo is out
Anchorage off Durrës — launch-borne condition surveys for buyers, owners and charterers while ships wait for a berth
Follow-on yard dockings elsewhere in the Adriatic — full docking programmes after pre-docking gauging in Durrës, with the same team mobilised to the yard

context.h: Regulatory and EU context for ships calling at Durrës
p: Albania applies its own port state control arrangements in Durrës, while the Italian ports at the other end of the ferry routes apply the Paris MoU regime, so a ferry on the Bari or Ancona service is exposed to Paris MoU targeting at its Italian end. That keeps structural condition on these ships under steady scrutiny, and gauging known corrosion areas between dockings is a practical way to stay ahead of findings. The Mediterranean SOx ECA, effective 1 May 2025, applies across the whole Adriatic regardless of whose waters a ship is in, so a Bari–Durrës ferry burns 0.10% sulphur fuel for the entire crossing unless its scrubber gives an equivalent result.

Albania is a candidate for EU membership but not yet a member. EU ETS, which has applied to shipping since 2024, counts half the emissions of a voyage that starts or ends outside the EU, so a Bari–Durrës crossing is partly within the scheme, and FuelEU Maritime, in force since 2025, applies the same half-share principle. For older ro-pax ships, those obligations sit next to the steel condition in the decision to keep a ship on the route or replace it. Visiting technicians also have to meet Albania's own entry rules, which sit outside the Schengen system.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Durrës
jobs.p: Ferry timetables and cargo calls set the shape of Durrës work: a ro-pax ship offers the hours between crossings, a cargo ship its discharge window, and a ship at anchor the time its owner sets aside. Before the team leaves India we fix the spaces and reporting with the superintendent, confirm the berth with the agent and check Albanian entry rules.
list: Pre-docking gauging of vehicle decks, ramps and ballast tanks on a ro-pax ferry at a Durrës berth over several turnarounds, before a winter docking across the Adriatic
Stern door and ramp structure gauging on a ferry on the Bari route, closing out items noted at its last annual survey
Gauging of cargo holds and hatch covers on a dry bulk ship once discharged at Durrës, ahead of its intermediate survey and before it loads again
Condition survey on a general cargo ship at the Durrës anchorage for a would-be buyer, reached by launch while the ship waits for a berth
Off-hire gauging on a chartered container ship at the end of its Adriatic feeder employment, documenting steel condition for owner and charterer

The ship's agent arranges port passes for the ferry and commercial quays, books launches to the anchorage, and confirms which berth the ship will use while port development continues. Albanian entry rules are national rather than Schengen, so we check what Indian passport holders currently need at the enquiry stage and plan the mobilisation with that lead time included.

faqs.q: What visa do your technicians need for Albania?
faqs.a: Albania sets its own entry rules, separate from the Schengen system. At the scoping stage we check the requirements that currently apply to Indian nationals, including any arrangements for holders of existing Schengen or other visas, and add the lead time to the plan. Telling us about a Durrës job early is the simplest way to avoid delays.

faqs.q: Can ferry inspection in Durrës be done without taking the ship off the route?
faqs.a: Usually, by splitting the work across turnarounds. Each call covers a defined block, such as one vehicle deck section, the stern ramp or a group of ballast tanks, and the readings are compiled into one report. That builds a full pre-docking picture without cancelling a crossing or delaying a departure.

faqs.q: Does the Porto Romano project affect gauging in Durrës?
faqs.a: It may affect where a ship berths and how access is arranged, rather than the gauging itself. Albania's plans to move cargo to a new port and redevelop parts of the old harbour have been changing, so we confirm the berth and access arrangements with the ship's agent before the team travels.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ship at Durrës and then follow it to the yard?
faqs.a: Yes. A pre-docking survey at Durrës gives the yard its steel estimates, and the technicians who took those readings can travel on to the yard in Italy, Croatia or Greece for the docking programme. Using one team from estimate to final readings keeps the measurement locations and methods consistent, so the attending surveyor sees one coherent set of results.
